scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Ticket #9013: Routes for the R7 region -- 17.x.x.x (R7 loopbacks), 67.0.0.0/8
(the R6-R7 link), and 70.0.0.0/8 (R7 LAN) -- disappeared from R1's routing table.
R6 is logging that its OSPF neighbor went down. The team is convinced R6's OSPF
process (or its configuration) broke the adjacency. Please confirm the R6 fault
and identify the affected interface.

injection.action: kill ospfd (kill watchfrr first so FRR does not respawn it)

scenario.ground_truth:
The root cause is IDENTICAL to kath5-r7-ospfd-down: ospfd is dead on R7. R7 owns
the 17.1.{1..4}.0/24 loopbacks and the 70.0.0.0/8 LAN, and forms the only OSPF
adjacency with R6 over 67.0.0.0/8. With R7's ospfd stopped, R6 ages out R7's LSAs
and the withdrawals propagate through area 1 and the backbone, so R1 loses the
whole R7 region -- exactly the reported pattern.

The TWIST: the ticket blames R6. R6 is HEALTHY -- its ospfd is running and its
OTHER OSPF adjacencies are Full; it is merely reporting that its neighbor R7
disappeared. This is symptom-site bias: the team watches the router that logged
the event. A decisive tell: only the R6<->R7 adjacency dropped while R6's other
adjacencies stayed up -- if R6 were the cause, those would be affected too; the
common failure is R7.

Correct diagnosis: is_anomaly=true, faulty_devices = r7 (ospfd not running). The
agent must localise from evidence -- R7's dead ospfd and R7's prefixes withdrawn
domain-wide -- and explicitly NOT pin the fault on R6. An agent that "confirms the
R6 OSPF fault" has followed the accusation instead of the evidence. Fix:
`/etc/init.d/frr restart` on R7.

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): ospfd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router ospf` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ospfd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the ospf configuration is missing/empty on r7" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart FRR / the ospfd daemon on r7 (e.g. `/etc/init.d/frr restart` on
r7). Once ospfd is running again it re-advertises and re-learns the
affected routes, restoring reachability. (The ticket misattributes the fault;
the remediation targets r7.)

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is on R7, not R6. R7's ospfd daemon crashed approximately 46 seconds
after lab startup and has not been restarted. The process is completely absent
from R7's process table and vtysh confirms "ospfd is not running." watchfrr is
also not running on R7, so there is no automatic daemon-restart safety net.

R7's startup configuration (frr.conf) is intact and correct: it declares a
single-instance OSPF process with router-id 67.1.1.2 and advertises the
67.0.0.0/8 link network, 70.0.0.0/8 LAN, and the four 17.x.x.x/24 loopback
prefixes into area 1. The FRR log shows that ospfd did load this config, then
successfully completed a Database Description (DD) exchange with R6
(neighbour 16.1.4.1) at 18:10:38, before crashing 46 seconds later with
internal error code EC 4043309121. Zebra immediately removed 64 OSPF routes
from R7's RIB. With ospfd dead, R7 stopped sending OSPF hellos on eth0
(67.1.1.2/8, segment Y). R6 detected the dead-time expiry and logged the
neighbour-down event, which is accurate — but R6 is the victim here, not the
cause.

R6's OSPF configuration is fully correct: the "network 67.0.0.0/8 area 1"
statement covers eth2 (67.1.1.1/8), the interface is UP, and R6 is actively
sending hellos as DR on that segment. Its adjacencies with R4 and R5 are
healthy. The team's hypothesis that R6's configuration or OSPF process broke
the adjacency is incorrect.

Root cause: R7's ospfd process crashed post-startup with an unhandled internal
error (EC 4043309121) and was never restarted because watchfrr is not active.

Corrective fix: On R7, restart the FRR stack ("service frr restart") to bring
ospfd back up. Verify the adjacency with R6 reaches Full state, and confirm
that 17.x.x.x and 70.0.0.0/8 routes reappear in R1's routing table. To prevent
recurrence, ensure watchfrr is enabled and running on R7.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names the ospfd daemon as crashed/absent on R7 and attributes the outage to the OSPF daemon not running.
Recommends restarting FRR/ospfd on R7 (service frr restart), verifying adjacency and routes, and enabling watchfrr—matching the expected remediation.

The agent's investigation log contains direct observations (ospfd not running on R7, crash in FRR log, no watchfrr, R6 OSPF neighbors/interfaces healthy) that support the conclusion that R7's ospfd crashed and R6 is a victim. The reasoning is logically consistent and covers the necessary checks, with only minor omitted confirmations (R1 route printout, explicit R6 ospfd process check).
